summary: Adds Bidirectional Reliable mode to the zero-byte profile of link-layer assisted RObust Header Compression, which RFC 3242 defined only for the unidirectional and optimistic modes. Zero-byte compression exists so a voice stream over certain older radio links is not pushed into a larger fixed packet size by even a one-byte compression header.

eli5.summary: Phone calls get chopped into little boxes of fixed size. Adding even one tiny label can make a box too big. This note shows a way to shrink the labels to nothing, in one more mode.

questions: what is a no-header packet in rohc
subtitle: Lets the link-layer assisted ROHC profile send voice packets with no compression header at all, now in Reliable mode too.

tldr.problem: On certain older radio links a voice packet has a fixed size, and even the single-octet ROHC header can push a packet into the next larger size. RFC 3242 removed that octet only for U-mode and O-mode.
tldr.mechanism: In R-mode the compressor may send a No-Header Packet (NHP) in place of a ROHC R-0 packet. The assisting layer decides when this is safe, using acknowledged sequence numbers, and the receiver works out the RTP sequence number from the last update packet.
tldr.outcome: Zero-byte compression now works in all three ROHC modes. The RFC says R-mode loses no robustness compared with ROHC RTP, because NHPs do not update either context.

today: RFC 3408 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds directly on RFC 3242.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This RFC extends the link-layer assisted RObust Header Compression (ROHC) profile, also called the zero-byte profile, from RFC 3242. Zero-byte compression exists so that the single-octet ROHC header does not push a packet voice stream into the next higher fixed packet size for the radio. It is usable in certain widely deployed older air interfaces.

RFC 3242 covers only Unidirectional (U-) and Bidirectional Optimistic (O-) modes. This document adds Bidirectional Reliable (R-) mode. The compressor in R-mode may deliver a No-Header Packet (NHP) when RFC 3242 would have required a ROHC Reliable Packet Type Zero (R-0) packet from RFC 3095.

The document is written as additions and exceptions to RFC 3242, and all its terminology is taken from there.
sections.eli5: An earlier note showed how to send voice packets with no label in two modes. This one adds a third mode, so the trick works everywhere.

sections.title: Assisting Layer Interface Additions
sections.content:
The profile adds parameters to the compressor to assisting layer (AL) interface from RFC 3242. Mode says which mode the compressor is in, and SN_ACKed gives the latest RTP sequence number that has been acknowledged; it is used only in R-mode. Both MUST be attached to every packet delivered to the AL.

There is also an optional interface from the AL back to the compressor, carrying an update_request. Implementing it is RECOMMENDED, for cases where the AL often finds it unsafe to send NHPs. Here, unsafe means the AL cannot guarantee the receiver will decompress the RTP sequence number of the NHP correctly. The profile can still be used where such an interface is impossible.
sections.eli5: The part that sends packets is told which mode it is in and which packet the other side has confirmed. It can also ask for a fresh full label when it needs one.

sections.title: R-mode Operation
sections.content:
In R-mode the profile maps the R-0 packet to the NHP. R-0 is the only R-mode packet type that can be replaced with an NHP.

The receiving side works out the RTP sequence number of an NHP as SN_Ref_D + Offset_D. SN_Ref_D is the sequence number of the last update packet the decompressor received, and Offset_D is the offset between the NHP and that update packet. How to derive the offset depends on the link technology and must be specified by the implementation documents. Examples given are counting non-context-updating packets and loss indications since the last update, or using link timing when RTP sequence number and link timing map linearly.

On the sending side the AL follows the rule from section 4.1.1 of RFC 3242, with one change. When it becomes unsafe to send NHPs, the AL records the sequence number as SN_break. It resumes NHPs only when the rule is satisfied again and SN_ACKed > SN_break. R-mode relies on acknowledgements to synchronize contexts, and R-0 packets do not update the decompressor context, which is why the optimistic approach of U/O-mode is not used.

To meet that condition the AL can wait for the compressor to send a context-updating packet (for example R-0-CRC when the 6-bit sequence number wraps), or send an update_request carrying the last SN_break. On receiving one, the compressor SHOULD use a context-updating packet for its next packet. Passive waiting can take a long time in the worst case, so the request is RECOMMENDED. A lost request only delays the resumption of NHPs.

NHPs and packet loss indications in R-mode update neither the compressor nor the decompressor context, so the secure reference principle of RFC 3095 is unaffected. The RFC concludes there is no loss of robustness compared with ROHC RTP.
sections.eli5: The sender only drops the label when it is sure the receiver can still guess the packet number. If it gets unsure, it waits until the receiver confirms a newer packet, or asks for a full label to speed things up.

sections.title: Differences from U/O-mode
sections.content:
The RFC lists several ways R-mode differs from U/O-mode in this profile.

  • CRC replacement is not an issue, because R-0 packets carry no CRC field.
  • Periodic context verification needs no change from ROHC RTP. Sending R-0-CRC when the 6-bit sequence number wraps provides it implicitly.
  • The decompressor SHOULD NOT send CV-REQUEST, to avoid needless feedback overhead.
  • When a Context Check Packet (CCP) is used, the compressor SHOULD set the C-bit to 0 and not generate a 7-bit CRC if computation cost is a concern.
  • For acknowledgements, it is RECOMMENDED to avoid interspersed feedback packets to carry ACK information, since they interrupt the RTP sequence numbering and temporarily disable NHPs.
sections.eli5: Some safety checks used in the other modes are not needed here, and one kind of reply message should be avoided because it would interrupt the label-free packets.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has reserved a ROHC profile identifier for this profile: 0x0105. The identifier assigned for the LLA profile in RFC 3242 is 0x0005.

The security considerations of ROHC RTP in RFC 3095 apply, with one addition. An intruder could inject bogus CCP packets with random CRC values. The CRC check would then fail for the wrong reasons at the decompressor, causing unnecessary context invalidation, feedback messages and refresh packets, and greatly reducing the advantages of ROHC and of this profile. The RFC notes that the same remarks about the presence of such an intruder apply.
sections.eli5: A troublemaker could send fake check messages that make the receiver throw away good information, which wastes the savings.
